title: Cisco Secure Client / AnyConnect Posture Agent Heartbeat and Version Drift
exclusions: Covers the detection logic documented for 'Cisco Secure Client / AnyConnect Posture Agent Heartbeat and Version Drift' only. Does not replace full NAC policy design or firewall rule authoring or regulatory attestation. Entities listed in `network_exception_register.csv` during approved tests are excluded.
evidence: Saved search `network_cisco_secure_client_anyconnect_posture_agent_hea` (UC-17.1.54), SOC dashboard panel "Network — Cisco Secure Client / AnyConnect Posture Agent Heartbeat and Version Drift", and weekly export to `index=audit_evidence` sourcetype=csv:network_controls.

compliance.assurance_rationale: PCI 5.3 — anti-malware mechanisms must be operational. Agent heartbeat evidences operational status.
compliance.evidenceArtifact: UC-17.1.54 alert log + monthly agent-coverage report.

compliance.assurance_rationale: A.8.7 — protection against malware via active agent.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Ingest synthetic events into `index=nac` sourcetype='cisco:ise:syslog' that satisfy the UC-17.1.54 SPL filters for 'Cisco Secure Client / AnyConnect Posture Agent Heartbeat and Version Drift'. Run the saved search and confirm at least one alertable row with expected fields populated.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Ingest benign `nac` / `cisco:ise:syslog` events outside the detection threshold, or exclude the test entity via `network_exception_register.csv` with a valid window. Confirm zero alert rows for UC-17.1.54.

dataSources: ISE syslog `index=nac sourcetype=cisco:ise:syslog` *Posture* category — codes `15050` (posture agent heartbeat), `15051` (posture agent version reported), `15052` (posture agent missing/timeout), `15053` (posture agent unsupported version), `15054` (posture agent stale config). Endpoint inventory feed from ISE OpenAPI `/api/v1/endpoint` polled hourly. Fields: `endpoint_mac`, `agent_version`, `agent_state`, `last_heartbeat`. Cisco Secure Endpoint API is the parallel feed.
spl:
(index=nac sourcetype="cisco:ise:syslog" MessageCode IN (15050, 15051, 15052, 15053))
  OR (index=nac sourcetype="cisco:ise:endpoint_inventory")
| stats count, latest(_time) as last_seen, latest(agent_version) as version, latest(agent_state) as state by endpoint_mac
| eval days_since_heartbeat = round((now() - last_seen) / 86400, 1)
| where days_since_heartbeat > 7 OR state=="timeout" OR like(version, "4.10%") OR like(version, "4.9%")
description: Detects endpoints whose posture agent (Cisco Secure Client / AnyConnect) hasn't sent a heartbeat for >7 days OR is running a deprecated/unsupported version. Both conditions break the posture trust loop.
value: Without an active posture agent, ISE has no way to validate endpoint compliance — it falls back to a default posture decision, typically less restrictive. Detecting agent absence at scale highlights the deployment gap (devices not yet enrolled, devices retired but still in inventory, or devices the install team missed).
implementation: Confirm *Posture* category at INFO. Endpoint-inventory poller every 1h. Schedule the search daily at 06:00 UTC.
visualization: (1) Single value: endpoints with stale heartbeat. (2) Bar chart: agent version distribution. (3) Top-N: device-types missing agents.
knownFalsePositives:
1. **Certificate or EAP profile rollout** — Clients fail EAP-TLS during staged cert deployment for 'Cisco Secure Client / AnyConnect Posture Agent Heartbeat and Version Drift'. Cross-check `FailureReason` and CMDB cert expiry.

2. **RADIUS/PSN maintenance restart** — Short auth failure burst while ISE node restarts. Match change window on `index=changes`.

3. **Guest or IoT onboarding surge** — Legitimate MAC registration spike skews `index=nac` `cisco:ise:syslog` baselines.

4. **Approved pen-test or scanner traffic** — Red-team exercises from netblock in `approved_scanners.csv` mimic auth failures.

**Suppression mechanism:** `network_exception_register.csv` keyed on `CallingStationID`, `NAS-IP-Address`, `valid_until`.
mitreAttack: N/A (agent fleet health — measures AnyConnect posture agent heartbeat, no attack mapping)
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Cisco Secure Client / AnyConnect deployed to endpoints.
• ISE *Posture* category at INFO.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Validate event flow.

Step 2 — Create the search
Search in `spl` field. Schedule daily.

Step 3 — Validate
Provoke as above.

Step 4 — Operationalize
Dashboard "ISE — Posture Agent Coverage":
• Single value: endpoints with stale heartbeat.
• Version distribution.
• Top-N missing.

Monthly review: agent-coverage report.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting
• **High count of stale heartbeats** — Mass-decommission scenario; clean inventory.
• **All on old version** — Agent-update mechanism broken.
• **Heartbeat events absent** — *Posture* category at WARN.

Step 1 — Configure data collection

Install and configure the add-on referenced in the app field (`Splunk Add-on for Cisco Identity Services` ([Splunkbase 1915](https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/1915)).). Enable the modular input or HEC token that writes sourcetype=cisco:ise:syslog, cisco:ise:endpoint_inventory into nac. Default poll interval 300–900 seconds unless the vendor API rate-limits lower. Grant the ingestion role `list_inputs` and `search` on the target index.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages. Document tunable macros in the comment header. Understanding this SPL: filters in the first pipeline reduce license cost; stats/timechart aggregates define the alert grain; joins/lookups enrich owner or asset metadata for routing.

Step 3 — Validate

Compare `| tstats count where index=... sourcetype=...` against the vendor admin UI inventory count (+/-5%). Spot-check two known entities for field presence (`days_since_heartbeat, endpoint_mac`). Run `timechart count span=1h` over 7 days to find ingestion gaps longer than two poll intervals.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Add a dashboard row with single-value KPI tiles, a 24-hour timechart, and a drilldown table mirroring the SPL output columns. Route critical severity to the platform on-call channel; route warning to the service owner from the lookup.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

No events: verify forwarder connectivity, HEC token ACLs, and that the modular input appears in `index=_internal source=*splunkd*`. NULL fields: check props/transforms order and TA version. Fewer results than expected: confirm index allow-lists on the search head role and that `_time` uses the correct timezone. API errors: inspect splunkd.log for HTTP 401/429 from the vendor endpoint configured in inputs.conf.
grandmaExplanation: Each company computer runs a small program that tells ISE 'I'm OK'. We watch for computers that have stopped saying 'I'm OK' for over a week — they may be off, retired, or compromised.
